The FOSS build does not send crash reports automatically. Redacted fatal and non-fatal reports are stored only in the app’s internal directory, with a maximum of 20 reports retained for 30 days. Reports are exported only when the user requests it through the system picker.
The FOSS build receives push through a secure socket connection and does not use Firebase Cloud Messaging.
The FOSS build receives notifications through a persistent secure connection. Android shows a service notification while standalone push is enabled.
Highlights are evaluated once when a message is received. Rules can highlight a row, play a sound, show an Android notification, and add an entry to the combined mentions list.
The Ferventio Server host cannot be empty
Ignore rules are applied before highlights: a fully hidden or collapsed message does not produce a sound, notification, or new Mentions entry.

OAuth tokens are not included in user backups. The opaque server session, device secret, and current Twitch access token are encrypted with an Android Keystore key; the Twitch refresh token is stored only on the configured server. The saved access token allows direct Twitch access to continue while the server is temporarily unavailable, until the Twitch token expires or is revoked.

The production Play build may send sanitized crash details, the app version, build type, push transport, and technical device and OS data to Firebase Crashlytics. Debug, benchmark, and FOSS builds do not enable automatic Crashlytics reporting.
